title: OneDrive: convert a Copilot response into a Word file on the web
summary: Hold: removing the whole Copilot licence is not the only documented way to restrict Copilot in OneDrive. Microsoft documents disabling its SharePoint service plan, which also disables Copilot in SharePoint; the licensing model also misclassifies an option within an existing licensed product as a separate add-on.

claims.claim: The new OneDrive option is classified as add-on rather than included in the Copilot licence its host product already requires.
claims.quote: Page field: model: "add-on". Microsoft: "Copilot in OneDrive is bundled as a part of Microsoft Copilot and is always on for licensed users."
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to "included": this is a new option inside licensed Copilot in OneDrive, not a separately documented add-on. Retain the notes naming the Microsoft Copilot licence and its E7 or eligible-plan add-on acquisition options.

claims.where: controls[0]; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: No tenant-wide UI switch or API is documented for turning this conversion option on or off separately from Copilot in OneDrive.
claims.quote: Searched: OneDrive Copilot convert response Word document save file sensitivity label admin disable switch Set-SPOTenant; Copilot OneDrive disable administrator settings Graph Word conversion. Read Copilot overview, OneDrive FAQ and searched Set-SPOTenant for Copilot/convert/Word; no option-only control.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses reaches licence assignment.
claims.quote: go to the Users > Active users page. ... Select the row of the user ... In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. ... Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph PowerShell supports Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() to assign a user licence.
claims.quote: To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell. Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot licence assignment governs licensed Copilot capabilities generally, not just the conversion option.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot license | Required for licensed Microsoft Copilot capabilities

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Holding or withholding the whole Copilot licence is the only documented way to decide who can use this OneDrive capability.
claims.quote: Copilot in OneDrive can be disabled in your service plan by your administrator by unchecking Microsoft Copilot for SharePoint from the Microsoft 365 admin center > Turn apps and services on or off. Note that this will disable Copilot in both OneDrive and SharePoint.
claims.fix: Replace the exclusivity claim in Why it matters and Governance controls with: "Licence assignment is one documented lever. Microsoft also documents disabling the Microsoft Copilot for SharePoint service plan, which disables Copilot in both OneDrive and SharePoint." Cite the FAQ URL above. Replace the After rollout bullet with: "Decide whether withholding this option warrants restricting broader Copilot access; no conversion-only switch is documented."

claims.fix: Replace the first sentence with: "The planned conversion gives users a one-click way to turn a Copilot response into a Word document."

claims.claim: Copilot respects existing SharePoint and OneDrive permissions.
